correctness.rationale: If m is even then m^(2r+1) is divisible by 8, forcing X^2=2 mod 8, impossible. A solution at coefficient m^(2r+1) gives a base solution (x,y)=(X,m^r Z). For odd m, x,y odd and m=7 mod 8; eta=x+y sqrt(m), epsilon=eta^2/2=(x^2-1)+xy sqrt(m) is integral of norm 1. All odd eta^n/2^((n-1)/2) therefore give integral positive norm-two solutions. For each p|m, x^2=2 mod p forces p>=7 and p∤x. In Y_n binomial sum the j=0 term has valuation v_p(y)+v_p(n), while every higher term gains j v_p(m)-v_p(2j+1)>0 (since v_p(2j+1)<j); hence the exact valuation law, permitting index n=m^r(2j+1) and m^r|Y_n. This proves the iff and infinite families. I independently checked m=7 base (3,1) gives (11427,617) at r=1, and m=23 base (5,1) gives (15191131279719638885,137720427724123513); the resulting three powerful numbers form a progression. The n-th-power and infinite-m parameter claims follow algebraically, not from samples.
